tickets.title: MDM flow engine — DAG compiler (flow.py)
tickets.summary: A flow is a DAG of typed nodes (input | clean | union | resolve | output) that compiles to ONE nested DuckDB SQL query over Parquet — no per-row Python, no intermediate copies. The resolve node is the golden-record loop: dedup on a strong/natural identity key, per-attribute survivorship, and <field>__conflict flags for the stewardship queue.
tickets.context: Tableau-Prep-style master building on the existing derive.py idiom (every transform = one SQL expression). Reuses derive.compile_rule + derive.apply_normalizer for all clean-node field expressions, so Mapping-tab rules and flow rules are ONE vocabulary — a rule learned in either place works in both. Design goal named by the owner: line of sight — every step must be inspectable and explainable.
acceptance: compile_sql(flow, node_id, uri_fn) returns runnable DuckDB SQL for any node's OUTPUT; cycles raise ValueError('flow has a cycle at node …'); unknown node/type raises
input compiles to SELECT *, '<ds>' AS _source FROM read_parquet('<uri>') — provenance rides from the first touch
clean projects derive rules onto the master schema (unmapped fields → NULL), carries _source, ANDs optional row filters
union is UNION ALL BY NAME over its inputs (schema-aligned stack, order-independent)

resolve dedups on strong key (COALESCE(NULLIF(strong,''), natural)) else the normalized natural key; survivorship rules any | authority | frequency | recency | longest | min | max | sum; emits _rows, _sources, _source_list, and <field>__conflict per attribute
conflict_sql returns the stewardship queue: identities whose sources disagree on a field, with values, value↔source pairs ({v, src}), sources, row counts
propose_flow(entity, datasets, master_fields) seeds a full draft flow (input→clean per feeding source →union→resolve→output) from landed data
identity normalization is PER-ENTITY config (_ENTITY_KEYS) — zero product logic hardcoded in the resolver
implementation: unifyd/flow.py, pure stdlib + derive. Key seams: _key_part(spec) — a key component is {field, norm} (norm defaults compare_form), compiled via derive._apply_transform; _identity_inner(node, upstream_sql) — attaches the resolve node's identity as _id, and is THE ONE basis shared by resolve's GROUP BY, conflict_sql, and provenance_sql so the three can never disagree about what merged; _survivor_sql(col, rule, auth_expr, recency_col) — rule → aggregate; _authority_case(sources) — CASE _source WHEN … mapping best-first order to descending ranks, 0 for unlisted

Survivorship SQL per rule: any → any_value(c) FILTER (WHERE nonblank); authority → arg_max(c, CASE-rank) FILTER nonblank; frequency → mode(c); recency → arg_max(c, recency_col) FILTER nonblank; longest → arg_max(c, length(CAST c AS VARCHAR)); min/max/sum → agg(try_cast(c AS DOUBLE)). Conflict flag: count(DISTINCT CAST(c AS VARCHAR)) FILTER (WHERE <>'') > 1

BUG FOUND+FIXED (data loss, the canonical match anti-pattern): SQL `a || b || c` is NULL if ANY part is NULL, so a row missing one key component silently VANISHED from the master — the end-to-end smoke test caught tx_outlets contributing zero golden records. Fix: every key part wraps COALESCE(<norm(col)>, ''), and the resolve filters WHERE replace(_id,'␟','') <> '' — drop only ALL-empty keys, never partial ones. Key components join on the ␟ separator

BUG FOUND+FIXED (false merge): identity originally ran every natural-key field through derive.identity_expr, which strips product edition tokens (holiday, seasonal, limited…). Applied to outlets, 'Holiday Wine & Spirits' would lose 'holiday' and could collide with another 'Wine & Spirits'. Fix: _ENTITY_KEYS gives each entity its own normalizer set — product: identity_key (vintage/edition stripping is CORRECT there); outlet: compare_form + address_core + zip5(none); party: strip_entity_suffix. Strong keys: product=upc, outlet=source_ref, party=None

HONESTY RENAME: the 'first' survivorship rule is actually any_value (arbitrary order in DuckDB) — renamed 'any' and documented; a deterministic tie-break for authority/frequency ties (secondary sort on source rank) is an open follow-up, noted in MDM_FLOW.md

propose_flow: score_dataset = share of the entity's identity fields auto_map can fill (threshold 0.34); every clean node projects the FULL master schema (unmapped → {mode:'expr', expr:'NULL'}) so union aligns; single-source flows skip the union node; auto_map is synonym-table driven (_SYNONYMS) with first-claim-wins per master field

DECISION (identity name mapping): a source's trade_name feeds outlet_name (the MATCH name — many sources carry only a trade name) and dba is reserved for an explicit doing-business-as column; before this, tx.trade_name landed on dba, leaving outlet_name NULL and the TX rows keyless (caught by the same smoke test)
verification: python3 unifyd/flow.py self-test green against real DuckDB 1.5.4: two-source fixture (s1: Titos 750ML/750 ML origin A ×2 rows; s2: Titos 750ml origin B) → 1 golden with _rows=3, _sources=2; size_ml normalized to 750 by all → size_ml__conflict false; origin A vs B → conflict true, authority s1>s2 survives A; conflict queue returns values [A,B] AND pairs {v,src} covering both sources; provenance returns the 3 constituent rows; profile lands (_n=1); catch-all test: 4 filled → 3 flagged ('Other','OTHER','misc'), 1 informative; cycle guard raises; product-vs-outlet key compile asserts ('gift set' present in product key SQL, absent in outlet key SQL); outlet seed maps DBA→dba + Owner Name→outlet_name with strong=source_ref

tickets.title: MDM_FLOW.md — the design canon (laws, cascade, personas, generalization, standard)
tickets.summary: The canon of record for the MDM build — the laws the code must obey, updated in the same commits as the behavior they govern. Downstream repos (canon-seed) sync their laws to THIS doc verbatim; a law changes here first, then propagates.
tickets.context: Written incrementally as each principle was decided with the owner, so every law carries its origin: (1) THE FIRST LAW — never fix the row, fix the rule: the golden record is a derivation, not a document; a row fix regenerates on the next pull, breaks reproducibility (an untraceable value = a restatement waiting to fire), destroys the lesson, and silently diverges from source; every steward action is a rule that re-materializes; a one-off is an override rule with provenance and a scope of one. (2) Real≠synthetic never commingle (separate namespaces, loud badge, never servable). (3) Identity from public first principles — no proprietary vendor IDs (an ethics decision by the owner re: VIP, and better architecture: portable, auditable, no lock-in). (4) The engine is domain-agnostic; a domain is a config pack — bev-alc is unique in field requirements, not tool capacity (the 'syndicate the lettuce industry' test: produce = UPC→PLU, TTB→PACA, one _ENTITY_KEYS row, zero engine changes). (5) Two personas — end user needs trust-at-a-glance; the steward LIVES here and needs line of ACTION, not just sight.
acceptance: Doc at repo root beside SPINE.md/BACKEND_DESIGN.md; every section marked 'as implemented' matches shipped endpoints/files

THE AUTOMATCH STANDARD stated accuracy-first (owner's correction, commit 4df4286): 90–95% is NOT a quota — accuracy is the binding constraint and automation is maximized subject to it; the rate is EARNED through better tiers (normalizers, evidence, authorities), never bought by loosening thresholds; the 5–10% human residue is the design working; measured as the PAIR — auto/claude-verified/oracle-resolved/human shares per entity per build AND false-merge precision by audit sampling
implementation: Sections and their content: the verification cascade (T0 deterministic → T1 Claude-verify: fetch the FACT from a whitelist of authoritative sources, verdict+evidence+confidence, never a similarity vote → T2 external oracle: Google Places = oracle-NOT-store, persist only the decision + durable place_id, never the payload; 'one open, one closed' resolves a same-address name conflict → T3 human, last and rarest)

Catch-all→COLA verify triggers (owner-specified): RECORD-level lazy-entry — once a record reaches the identifier level (resolvable to a COLA product cluster), fire if ≥40% of its RESPONDED fields are catch-all (denominator = responded fields, isolating 'answered with a non-answer' from ordinary blankness; you identify on the clean fields and verify the junk); FIELD-level — dataset-wide catch-all share = source untrustworthy for that field. Backfill-empty silently; escalate specific-value conflicts with evidence (label wins as higher authority); provenance = TTB COLA + filing id

Split-case (repack) explosion: detection = multiple abbreviated brand tokens in one item field (a legit item doesn't carry two brands; abbreviation is a character-limit artifact — owner's field knowledge); size is a FACT TO FETCH, not a guess (Grey Goose spans 50ml–1.75L): total net volume constrains count×size → the physical-vs-9L-ACCOUNTING-case trap (never treat a 9L statistical case as a bottle count) → gross-weight backstop → repack-UPC → stored recipe (solve once, auto-split forever) → authoritative lookup → human; mixed-size cases end at the recipe or the human, so REMEMBERING beats solving live

The match/steward surface spec (two-pane, select-or-drag), the serve layer (real-only by construction), the edge-case catalog grounded in the real connectors (dba≠legal_name — NY legalname doubles as owner; premise vs mailing address — CT backer_address is the licensee's HQ/lawyer; licensee≠establishment — TX master_file_id; lifecycle — new operator at same address after a gap = NEW outlet + old closed, Google open/closed resolves it), and the common-strings table that became HS-003
verification: Cross-read against shipped code at each merge; canon-seed/CLAUDE.md laws diffed against this doc after the accuracy-first reframe

tickets.title: Common-string normalizers in derive.py — the edge-case catalog, banked as code
tickets.summary: Eight reusable SQL transforms for the recurring dirt in outlet/party data, registered in derive.TRANSFORMS so they work in every rule, every flow clean node, and every identity key — each self-tested against live DuckDB rows.
tickets.context: Owner's directive: 'keep pressing on edge cases — it's how a model is actually built; find the common strings and address them.' The catalog was mined from the REAL connectors (master.py colmaps, socrata_outlets, ct_dcp, tx_tabc), not invented: legal-suffix noise in licensee-name sources, hand-keyed placeholders, USPS drift, chain store numbers, unicode/punctuation variance.
acceptance: null_if_placeholder: N/A · NA · N.A. · NONE · NULL · SAME · SEE ABOVE · UNKNOWN · UNK · TBD · . · 0 · 00 · XXX · X · -- · --- (and blank) → NULL; real values pass through

strip_entity_suffix: 'SMITH ENTERPRISES LLC' → 'SMITH ENTERPRISES'; 'John Smith Inc' → 'JOHN SMITH'; 'COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP' → 'COSTCO WHOLESALE' (handles L L C, INCORPORATED, LLP, LP, LTD, LIMITED, PLLC, PC; dots/commas pre-stripped)
address_std: '123 Main Street' → '123 MAIN ST'; '456 North Ave.' → '456 N AVE' (USPS token standardization)
address_core: '789 Oak Blvd Ste 400' → '789 OAK BLVD' (secondary-unit clause removed → the building-level block key); unit_ext: same input → '400'
store_no_ext / name_no_store: 'WALMART #1234' → '1234' / 'WALMART' (patterns: #, STORE, STR, NO. + 2–6 digits)
compare_form: 'Barnes & Noble' → 'BARNES AND NOBLE'; 'Café Ñoño' → 'CAFE NONO' (strip_accents, &→AND, punctuation dropped, whitespace collapsed)
implementation: Templates authored with an '@@' column placeholder for legibility, then registered into TRANSFORMS as %s templates (the registry's existing convention). _STREET_STD (~20 tokens: street types, directionals incl. compounds, unit designators) applies LONGEST-TOKEN-FIRST so NORTHEAST→NE replaces before NORTH→N — order is load-bearing
SCOPE HONESTY: _STREET_STD is a ~20-token subset of the ~200-entry USPS suffix table; PO-box detection and the premise-vs-mailing merge guard are deliberately NOT here — widened + hardened in HS-016

These feed _ENTITY_KEYS (HS-001): outlet identity = compare_form(outlet_name) ␟ address_core(address) ␟ zip5 — which is exactly what let '123 Main St' merge with '123 Main Street' in the endpoint smoke test
verification: python3 unifyd/derive.py green — every transform evaluated against live DuckDB rows with the exact example strings above; existing 6-mode compile tests unchanged and green

tickets.title: /api/flow/* endpoints — the engine, reachable and sampled
tickets.summary: Nine endpoints wiring flow.py to the browser. Every read is sampled/aggregated INSIDE DuckDB — a full table is never materialized into Python — so line-of-sight stays instant as sources grow.
tickets.context: Routes (all under the existing auth gate + rate limit): GET /api/flow/datasets (input palette from Parquet FOOTERS only — rows+schema, never data); GET/POST /api/flow (persist flows to agent_state/flows.json, id minted flow_#####); POST /api/flow/seed {entity} (propose_flow over landed datasets + the entity's saved master schema); POST /api/flow/preview {flow,node,limit≤500}; POST /api/flow/profile {flow,node,sample} (fill/distinct/catch-all per column); POST /api/flow/sql (the Explain view); POST /api/flow/conflicts {flow,node,field,limit≤500}; POST /api/flow/provenance {flow,node,id} (HS-008); POST /api/flow/run (materialize + mint Hoodie IDs).
acceptance: seed → a full draft flow + dataset count; unknown/empty warehouse degrades to a note, never a 500
profile excludes internal columns (_-prefixed AND __conflict), caps at 40 columns, returns filled/distinct/catchall/fill_pct/informative_pct per field

run: SELECT DISTINCT _id from the compiled node → registry mint HO-<pfx>-%06d (prefixes: outlet=O, product=I, party=P) → TEMP TABLE _homap join → COPY (SELECT m.hoodie_id, q.* …) TO '<table>.parquet'; response carries rows, hoodie_minted, hoodie_total
Hoodie IDs are STABLE: the registry (agent_state/hoodie_ids.json, identity-signature → id) is consulted before minting; a rebuild reuses every existing id
every endpoint returns ok:true with a bounded error string on failure (degrade honestly — no stack traces to the client)
implementation: server.py section '── MDM Flow ──' placed above the static-serving block. _flow_compile(body) resolves node (defaults to the flow's last node) and compiles with the mode-bound uri resolver (mode added in HS-009). _flow_jsonsafe recursively converts DuckDB output: date/datetime→isoformat, Decimal→float, bytes→utf-8-replace, lists/dicts deep — needed because list(DISTINCT …) aggregates and Parquet dates otherwise break jsonify
FIX 5d77fba: the resolve node's <field>__conflict helper columns were rendering as profile cards (28 'fields' instead of 14) — filtered at the column-introspection step, verified in-browser
hoodie_ids.json shape after HS-009: {mode: {entity: {map: {identity→id}, next: int}}} — real and synthetic mint from SEPARATE id spaces
verification: End-to-end smoke (flask test_client + local Parquet warehouse, ab_outlets + tx_outlets fixtures): seed → 2 datasets, 7 nodes; preview at resolve → 3 golden from 4 source rows with Trader Joe's merged cross-source ('123 Main St' ≡ '123 Main Street' via address_core, _sources=2, _source_list=[tx_outlets, ab_outlets]); profile → 28→14 fields after fix; run → dim_outlet with hoodie_id column, 3 minted; SECOND run → hoodie_minted=0, hoodie_total=3 (stability proven, not asserted)

tickets.title: Catch-all detection — 'other' is populated-but-empty, and it screams
tickets.summary: The profile counts catch-all values per column and reports INFORMATIVE completeness (filled − catch-all). A field 100% filled but 80% 'other' now screams instead of passing every completeness metric.
tickets.context: Owner's formative scar (the VIP lazy-entry pattern): record-enterers fill the fields they need and dump the rest to 'other'. A catch-all is worse than NULL — NULL honestly says 'unknown'; 'other' LIES that the answer is known. It defeats completeness metrics (non-null ≠ informative), is a one-way information loss (you can't recover a category from 'other', and you'd never know to), poisons matching and rollups (indistinguishable from a real category), and bills the enterer's convenience to everyone downstream. 'Hoodie will never lose on accuracy.'
acceptance: _CATCHALL vocabulary (16 values: other, others, misc, miscellaneous, general, generic, unspecified, unknown, undefined, default, various, n/a, na, none, tbd, null) matched case-insensitively, trimmed
profile_sql emits count(*) FILTER (catch-all) AS <col>†other per column alongside †fill and †dct
/api/flow/profile returns catchall + informative_pct = (filled − catchall)/total per field
DECISION: catch-alls are COUNTED, never auto-nulled — some are legitimate values; the measurement is the guard, nulling would be a silent row-fix of its own
implementation: flow.py: _catchall_pred(qcol) → lower(trim(CAST … AS VARCHAR)) IN (…); profile_sql keeps sampling support (USING SAMPLE n ROWS) so the scan stays bounded at scale

Downstream consumers already specced: HS-011's record-level trigger (≥40% of RESPONDED fields catch-all at identifier level → COLA label verify) and the UI thresholds (≥15% other → red card, <50% informative → amber) in HS-006
verification: Self-test: 4 filled values ('Vodka','Other','OTHER','misc') → fill=4, other=3, informative=1; in-browser on the synthetic outlet set: dba and city flag '38% other' red, honest 0%-filled fields flag amber

tickets.summary: apps/mdm-flow.html — the consolidated master-building workbench. Dense, mono-forward, keyboard-first — and on the suite's LIGHT base theme.

Re-skinned to the base tokens and fixed every hardcoded dark value (SQL pre text, profile bar empty-segment, toast, palette scrim, tag/chip colors, selection color). tickets.title: Resolvable conflicts — the steward picks the RULE, never the value
tickets.summary: The conflicts view became a workbench: per-field survivorship rule selector (any · authority · frequency · recency · longest), a promotable source-authority order, and the LIVE golden winner per contested record. Every gesture writes a rule that re-materializes — there is no control that edits a value. The first law, enforced by the UI's shape.
tickets.context: First law consequence: 'resolving' a conflict means choosing the rule that governs the field, not picking a value for one row. The engine change that makes resolution TRANSPARENT: conflict_sql now returns value↔source PAIRS — list(DISTINCT {'v': value, 'src': _source}) — so the steward sees exactly who said what before choosing whom to trust.
acceptance: Per contested field: rule selector writes flow.survivors[field]; authority bar shows the node's source order (best-first, rank chips), click promotes a source to #1 and writes flow.authority; both persist via POST /api/flow and the view re-queries
Live winner column (→ value) re-previews the resolve node keyed by _id, so a rule change updates the golden value in front of the steward
Setting outlet_name → authority with tx_outlets promoted deterministically flips the winners to the tx values (TRADER JOES, TWIN LIQUORS)
implementation: flow.py: conflict_sql adds the pairs aggregate; self-test asserts pairs cover {A,B}×{s1,s2}. UI (mdm-flow.html): loadConflicts probes every resolve-node field via /api/flow/conflicts and shows only fields that actually disagree; setRule/promoteAuthority mutate the in-memory flow, saveFlow persists, view reloads

OBSERVED, WORTH KEEPING: fields left on 'any' visibly WOBBLED between two renders ('123 Main Street' → '123 Main St') because any_value is arbitrary-order — while the authority-ruled field held stable. The screenshots accidentally demonstrate the case for ruling every contested field: an unruled field is a coin flip per rebuild; a ruled field is defensible
verification: Self-test green (pairs assertion); Playwright drive: promote tx_outlets → set outlet_name=authority → before/after screenshots show the winner flip + the toast 'outlet_name → survive by authority · a rule, re-materializes'

tickets.title: Provenance drill-down — the evidence behind every golden value
tickets.summary: Click any golden record → a drawer showing, per field, the golden value beside each constituent source row's value, with the WINNING source highlighted green. 'Here are the rows it came from' — not 'trust me'. The trust surface that makes zero-restatements defensible.
tickets.context: Refactor that makes it correct-by-construction: identity extraction was centralized as _identity_inner(), THE single basis used by resolve's GROUP BY, conflict_sql, and the new provenance_sql — so provenance can never display rows that didn't actually merge into that golden record (they share the same _id computation by definition, not by convention).
acceptance: POST /api/flow/provenance {flow, node, id} → the golden row + up to 80 constituent upstream (pre-resolve) rows filtered WHERE _id = ?

Resolve-node Data rows are clickable (hint shown); drawer renders a field × (golden | source…) matrix; cell highlighted green when it equals the golden value (the winner); ∅ for empties; Esc / scrim / ✕ close
Drawer title falls back through outlet_name → dba → brand → first field → id
implementation: flow.py: provenance_sql(flow, resolve_node_id, uri_fn) = _identity_inner over the compiled upstream; server.py endpoint also fetches the golden row (compiled resolve SQL WHERE _id = ?) so the matrix has its comparison column; _flow_jsonsafe covers the list-typed _source_list
verification: Self-test: 3 upstream rows share the 1 golden's _id; in-browser TWIN LIQUORS drill: 2 source rows → 1 golden; outlet_name + address highlighted under tx_outlets (authority winner), city green under BOTH sources (they agree — Austin), license_num from tx only, empties honest ∅

tickets.title: Real/synthetic isolation + the real-only serve API (the syndication gate)
tickets.summary: Warehouse namespaces every dataset by mode (real/ vs synthetic/); a build reads exactly ONE namespace; Hoodie IDs mint from per-mode id spaces; and /api/serve/<entity> + /api/serve/<entity>/<hoodie_id> are REAL-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION (mode hardcoded server-side) — synthetic can never reach a consumer, not by policy but by code shape.
tickets.context: Owner's requirement, twice over: 'you need to isolate real and synthetic… I can't do anything in Hoodie Intelligence' (a number whose realness you can't tell is a number you can't act on — commingling is how an analytics surface dies), and the serve question ('should we think about how to serve to Unifyd? API?') made isolation the non-negotiable GATE on syndication. The stable Hoodie ID is the consumer's join key — the ID is the product.
acceptance: warehouse.py: uri/query/list_datasets/write_parquet all take mode; _seg() maps mode → path segment (local subdir, S3 key prefix); mode=None preserves the legacy flat namespace so every pre-existing endpoint is untouched (backward-compatible by default)

server.py: _flow_mode(body) validates to real|synthetic (default real); _flow_uri(mode) binds the compiler's uri resolver; ALL nine /api/flow/* endpoints thread mode; flow/run writes the output table INTO the mode namespace and mints from hoodie_ids.json[mode][entity]
/api/serve/<entity>?page=&size= (paged, ORDER BY hoodie_id) and /api/serve/<entity>/<hid> read mode='real' hardcoded — there is no parameter that can change it
UI: the REAL/SYNTHETIC badge is a functional toggle (green REAL / amber SYNTHETIC), injected into every POST body by the api() wrapper, default REAL, re-seeds on flip
implementation: Per-mode id spaces both start at HO-O-000001 and never collide because they live under separate registry keys — a deliberate choice: synthetic ids are as stable as real ones (demos survive rebuilds) but are meaningless outside their namespace
Serve pagination caps size at 500; missing table degrades to ok:true, landed:false with a bounded error
verification: End-to-end proof: wrote ab+tx fixtures into synthetic/, one real_outlets fixture into real/; list_datasets(synthetic)=[tx,ab], list_datasets(real)=[real_outlets], list_datasets()=[] (isolation physical); synthetic build → 2 golden (HO-O-000001..2 in synthetic space); real build → 1 golden (HO-O-000001 in real space); /api/serve/outlet → total=1, ONLY 'Bar Louie' — the synthetically-mastered Trader Joe's/Total Wine EXIST in synthetic/dim_outlet and were NOT servable; by-id lookup HO-O-000001 → Bar Louie

tickets.title: Two-pane match/steward page — source left, master right
tickets.summary: Record-level matching for the residue the identity key missed: source records on the left, golden masters on the right. Select 1+ left + 1 right → Match (multi-select = 'these are all this one real entity'), or DRAG a single source row onto a master. Plus 'not a match' (suppressed forever) and 'new master' (mint a fresh Hoodie ID). The owner specified this page's interaction model verbatim.
tickets.context: This is T3 of the cascade made concrete — and under the accuracy-first standard it should see only the 5–10% residue. Every decision is a persisted RULE that re-applies on rebuild (generalize the outlet_confirms.json pattern → match_decisions.json keyed by mode+entity; a decision is {a, b, verdict, at, by} where a/b are identity signatures, NOT row edits — first law). Filter both panes to a BLOCK (e.g. same address_core, or the jaro-winkler/geo candidate pairs from the existing Confirm SQL) so the steward compares like with like. Decisions feed back as tuning signal for the resolver's thresholds.
acceptance: Multi-select left + single right → assigns those source identity signatures to the master's hoodie_id; persists; SURVIVES a full re-run (the apply step is part of resolve)
Drag a left row onto a right row = the same assignment, one gesture
Reject persists and suppresses the pair from every future candidate queue; New-master mints from the per-mode registry
Decisions applied DURING resolve — a post-GROUP-BY id remap executed before Hoodie-ID mapping in flow_run_ep, so the golden output and serve API reflect them
Keyboard: j/k through candidate pairs, m match, x reject, n new-master — a steward works a 200-item queue without the mouse

tickets.title: Explode node + repack-recipe store — split mixed cases to the right SKUs
tickets.summary: Kit-to-component explosion: a distributor repack ('3 Grey Goose + 3 Bacardi', shipped as one real item with its own repack number/UPC) explodes into component lines matched to the right canonical SKUs, quantities fanned to the fact tables. A SECONDARY workflow (an explode node between clean and resolve), not the main resolve path.
tickets.context: Owner's spec, including the pressure test ('you know exactly what I'm saying but have no idea what size bottles were in that case'): DETECTION is aggressive — multiple (usually ABBREVIATED) brand tokens in one item field is the tell, because a legit single item doesn't carry two brands and the abbreviation is a character-limit artifact ('3 GG / 3 BAC'); lower the confidence threshold, run either a detector agent over the item stream or an explicit prompt callout, and expand abbreviations against the brand dictionary. SIZE IS A FACT TO FETCH, never a guess (Grey Goose spans 50ml–1.75L; guessing 750 is the bug): the cascade is (1) total net volume on the line — count × size constrained; (2) the PHYSICAL-vs-9L-ACCOUNTING-CASE trap — depletion 'cases' are often 9L statistical cases (12×750≡9L), never treat that count as bottles; (3) gross weight backstop (~0.95 kg/L separates 750ml from 1.75L); (4) repack UPC → STORED RECIPE — repacks recur, solve once and every later occurrence auto-splits; (5) authoritative lookup; (6) human — whose answer becomes the stored recipe so it never asks twice. Mixed-size cases (3×GG 750 + 3×Bacardi 1L) defeat the volume constraint and almost always end at the recipe or the human: REMEMBERING beats solving live.
acceptance: explode node between clean and resolve; BOM expansion emits component rows with quantities; provenance carries the repack id + resolution method

verification_plan: Fixtures: single-size case w/ total volume (deterministic split, no human); mixed-size case (routes to recipe/human, never guesses); recurring repack UPC (auto-split on second sight, telemetry shows tier=recipe); 9L accounting case (classified, not exploded as bottles)
